prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val][adversarial] Long group header over tiny sub-columns (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Merged cells: "Model" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Benchmark accuracy on he" spans 3 col × 1 row; "Notes" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Model" · longest unbreakable word 45px · one-line width 45px
  col 2: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › EN" · longest unbreakable word 21px · one-line width 21px
  col 3: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › ZH" · longest unbreakable word 22px · one-line width 22px
  col 4: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › AR" · longest unbreakable word 21px · one-line width 21px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 581px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare multilingual benchmark accuracy across three model sizes while providing practical notes about each model.","reading":"Readers scan each model row across EN, ZH and AR, compare scores down each language column, and consult the notes for context.","groups":["EN, ZH and AR are parallel accuracy measures under one benchmark header, so they should have equal widths.","Model identifies each row; Notes provides supporting prose for the same model."],"keep_intact":["Model names and language identifiers","Individual accuracy values","Unbreakable words in the notes"],"may_wrap":["The long benchmark group header can wrap across its three columns.","Notes can wrap at word boundaries; their wrapping can use row height created by other cells."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [85, 105, 105, 105, 319] · table 720×275px · row heights [60, 36, 83, 36, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [75, 75, 75, 75, 399] · table 700×252px · row heights [83, 36, 60, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 1/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [90, 135, 135, 135, 224] · table 720×299px · row heights [60, 36, 106, 36, 60] · column headers wrapped 1/6 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
